groups.name: Reasoning / General Intelligence
groups.question: Can it think through problems across domains?

recommended.name: MMLU
recommended.why: Broad academic and professional knowledge across many subjects.

recommended.name: GPQA
recommended.why: Graduate-level science questions that are hard for non-experts.

recommended.name: BIG-Bench Hard
recommended.why: A suite of challenging reasoning tasks selected from BIG-Bench.

recommended.name: ARC-AGI
recommended.why: Abstract pattern reasoning with less reliance on memorized text.

groups.name: Code And Data Work
groups.question: Can it debug, write analysis code, and work in notebooks?

recommended.name: SWE-bench / SWE-bench Verified
recommended.why: Real GitHub issue resolution; useful for tracking agentic coding.

recommended.name: DS-1000
recommended.why: Python data science code across pandas, NumPy, matplotlib, sklearn, and more.

recommended.name: DA-Code
recommended.why: Agentic data-analysis tasks using real datasets, executable code, and multi-step planning.

recommended.name: HumanEval+ / MBPP+
recommended.why: Cleaner code-generation signal, though less newsroom-like.

recommended.name: BIRD
recommended.why: Text-to-SQL over realistic databases.

groups.name: Data / Analytical Reasoning
groups.question: Can it reason over structured data, tables, charts, and calculations?

recommended.name: TableBench
recommended.why: Direct table QA, data analysis, numerical reasoning, and visualization.

recommended.name: TAT-QA
recommended.why: Questions over financial tables plus surrounding text.

recommended.name: ChartQA
recommended.why: Chart interpretation and visual reasoning.

recommended.name: FinQA
recommended.why: Financial numerical reasoning with executable programs.

groups.name: Truthfulness / Hallucinations
groups.question: Does it make things up, repeat myths, or know when not to answer?

recommended.name: TruthfulQA
recommended.why: Targets common misconceptions and imitative falsehoods.

recommended.name: SimpleQA
recommended.why: Short factual questions with single verifiable answers.

recommended.name: FEVER
recommended.why: Claim verification against evidence from Wikipedia.

recommended.name: HaluEval
recommended.why: Hallucination detection across QA, dialogue, and summarization.

groups.name: Unstructured → Structured Extraction
groups.question: Can it pull entities, categories, fields, and relationships out of messy documents?

recommended.name: DocIE
recommended.why: Document-level entity, mention, type, and relation extraction from long unstructured text.

recommended.name: IDP Leaderboard
recommended.why: Key information extraction, OCR, document classification, long-document processing, and table extraction.

recommended.name: FUNSD / CORD / SROIE
recommended.why: Older form, receipt, and key-value extraction benchmarks for semi-structured documents.

recommended.name: DocVQA / InfographicVQA
recommended.why: Question answering over visually structured documents.

groups.name: Tool Use / Agents
groups.question: Can it complete multi-step workflows with tools and external information?

recommended.name: GAIA
recommended.why: Real-world tasks requiring browsing, tools, planning, and multimodal reasoning.

recommended.name: BrowseComp
recommended.why: Persistent web research for hard-to-find but verifiable answers.

recommended.name: WebArena
recommended.why: Agents operating websites to complete realistic tasks.

recommended.name: OSWorld
recommended.why: Computer-use agents completing tasks in desktop environments.
